critiques: Curriculum A uses the extremely limited 45-minute budget much more effectively by focusing on hands-on, exam-oriented practical skills. It provides a more applied architecture video (which includes practical troubleshooting matching CKA symptoms) compared to B's purely theoretical analogy-based one. Curriculum A also manages to fit in a lesson on Deployments and ReplicaSets, plus a specific CKA 'trap' video regarding NodePorts. Curriculum B, on the other hand, wastes 13 minutes on a talking-head exam strategy video (rules, documentation tabs), which does not teach Kubernetes concepts or hands-on cluster setup. Both meet the 2023+ constraint using up-to-date and 2025-labeled videos for the hands-on portions, but A delivers significantly more technical value.

Curriculum A provides a more cohesive and balanced approach. It directly addresses the learner's request for CKA exam topics and orientation with a dedicated exam strategy video that covers rules, time management, and documentation techniques. Curriculum B makes an awkward timestamp cut in the imperative commands video (starting at 03:46) and skips the exam overview entirely in favor of piecemeal deployment videos. Curriculum A smoothly covers architecture, cluster setup, practical imperative commands, and exam strategy within the tight time budget.

Curriculum A perfectly aligns with the learner's goals and constraints. It provides hands-on, CKA-oriented content, covers imperative commands critical for the exam, and includes a modern (2025) kubeadm cluster setup walkthrough. It also avoids teaching what the learner already knows. Curriculum B wastes time on redundant, surface-level architecture overviews and a 'Docker vs Kubernetes' video, which violates the constraint of not re-teaching what the learner already knows. It also lacks any CKA exam focus or kubeadm setup.

Curriculum A violates multiple constraints: it wastes time re-teaching the difference between Docker and Kubernetes (which the learner already knows), covers architecture twice, and fails to include any kubeadm cluster setup or CKA-specific exam preparation. Curriculum B is perfectly tailored to the learner's goal. It focuses on CKA-specific tips, covers imperative commands essential for the exam, includes a recent (2025) kubeadm setup walkthrough, and efficiently introduces the core concepts without wasting time on redundant Docker basics.

Curriculum A makes much better use of the limited time budget by excluding the vlog in Curriculum B (Video 1, flagged as a vlog and pure theory). Instead, Curriculum A allocates that time to watch a longer, more substantial portion of the imperative commands video, which is highly practical and critical for passing the hands-on CKA exam. Both curricula hit the required topics (architecture, deployments, services, kubeadm), but Curriculum A avoids filler content.

Curriculum B is better because it avoids the low-value 'vlog' video used in Curriculum A, reallocating that time to the more practical imperative commands tutorial. Furthermore, Curriculum B uses verified transcript timestamps to select a specific segment for the imperative commands video, whereas Curriculum A blindly guesses the 0-9 minute range. Curriculum B's curation is much more precise and focused on actionable exam skills.
